subject: English
passage: Anthropologist Hannah Ellsworth and colleagues studied stone tools discovered in Ethiopia that are more than 2.8 million years old. The researchers determined that the stone tools belonged to two previously unknown hominin species. Moreover, they found that one of the two species had created tools with significantly more sophisticated crafting techniques than those used by Homo habilis, which was previously considered the earliest known toolmaker.
prompt: Based on the text, which choice best describes the two previously unknown hominin species?

choices.A: They lived more than 2.8 million years ago.
choices.B: They are frequently studied by anthropologists.
choices.C: They both used less sophisticated toolmaking techniques than Homo habilis did.
choices.D: They lived primarily in forested environments.

explanation: Choice A is the best answer because it presents a statement about the two previously unknown hominin species that is supported by the text. According to the text, the stone tools belonged to the two previously unknown hominin species and are more than 2.8 million years old. This indicates that the species must have existed more than 2.8 million years ago.
